title: Das ist peinlich…
body:
Mein Setup: iPhone 13pro
Uhr: Galaxy Watch

Performance der App: unterirdisch 

Die App braucht ewig bis sie mit der Uhr synchronisiert, wenn sie es mal nach gefühlt ewigen  2min (gemessen sind es 17-24 Sekunden)

Jedes mal wenn man versucht mit der App zu interagieren, braucht es 3-7 Sekunden.

Mehrmaliges zurücksetzten beider Geräte hat nichts geholfen.

Ich hatte in der Vergangenheit ein Samsung Smartphone und da sind Welten dazwischen.

Was Samsung als Werbung für seine Geräte nützen könnte (Wearable als Einstieg ins Samsung Universum) ist eher wohl eine Abschreckung.

Ich werde mich nach Smartphone auch von der Uhr trennen, auch wenn diese selbst tut was sie soll, aber die Software ist einfach nur schlecht und am User vorbei!

Welche Fehler bei den Updates behoben werden, frage ich mich auch schon lange, bei mir bestehen seit nunmehr 9 Monaten die gleichen Probleme in der App.
Am schlimmsten finde ich aber den App-Support - sollte eher Tagebuch heißen, weil man sich hier zwar zwecks Fehlermeldung detailliert den Frust und Ärger von der Seele schreiben kann, eine Antwort kriegt man aber doch nie.

title: Doesn’t stay connected to watch
body:
This app constantly disconnects from the watch and this is worse since the last update. Any time I want to take a look at my health data, the app says “no wearable device connected” and I have to reboot the watch in order for it to connect and transfer data. Every time now. It is ridiculously inconvenient to the point of defeating the purpose of having a wearable device with a “syncing” app.

I understand the limitations of staying connected to a Bluetooth device in the iOS environment, but that’s not really the issue. The frustrating thing is that the app will not recognise the watch on opening the app and a reboot is required for them to talk. I shouldn’t have to reboot the watch every time - it’s absurd. I doubt it’s an issue with connecting to the phone because the Samsung Watch app does not suffer the same issue; it stays connected just fine. This Health app is the problem.

I’d give the app four or five stars if it stayed connected as the features are quite good. However, those features are near useless if it will not retrieve the data.

title: Great update!
body:
The latest update for this app was great, thanks for including HR under the metrics when you have a Gear Fit 2 Pro connected. I'm looking at this app more than I look at my Apple Health app (because I want to buy a Gear Fit 2 Pro at some stage). Is there any chance you guys could add in stress and floors climbed into the metrics? And SPO2? Unless that's not possible due to the limitations of the iPhone (since it doesn't have a red light sensor like your phones do).

Anyway, thanks for working on this app for iPhone users, it is much appreciated!!!

Update: Thanks for sending me an email Samsung! The iPhone has a built in barometer, so that's why I wondered if you could build in floor tracking but it's good to know that it will work if you connect a Gear Fit 2 Pro. Thanks for following up on the stress and SPO2 measurements, there are apps that use the flash and camera to calculate heart rate on iPhone but I'm unsure if you need a special red light sensor like the one on Samsung phones to measure SPO2. Once again thanks for looking out for us iPhone folk, some of us are definitely intrigued by your wearables lineup!

title: Great app! A few issues...
body:
I purchased a Samsung Galaxy Fit watch a year ago, and I immediately downloaded this app. For the most part it has worked excellently for me, and I had no problems whatsoever. But I did have some problems, some of which defied the purpose of the app:

-There was a two-month period where the app didn’t track my heart rate at all. I have a huge gap in my tracking, and since this is the only way to keep my heart rate readings without writing them down, I found this especially annoying. It works now, but every now and again I will have a gap of a few days in my graph.

-You need a SIM Card to use the app. For a while my phone didn’t have a SIM Card, so I had to use the app on a device that wasn’t mine.

-I’m slightly confused about a certain feature. Stress tracking is something that is shown on the website for my watch, and in pictures of Samsung Health, but I don’t seem to have it. Is this because I am an IOS user?

-How come you can’t be below the age of thirteen to use this app? I noticed this a while back and it seems strange to me. There are kids who have Samsung products and who would happily use this app if they could put In their proper age.

All in all, great app. I would suggest it for anyone who wants to use it. Just a few problems. Thank you!

title: Disappointed in the accuracy
body:
I’d like to be able to record portions that I eat, but the app doesn’t give me the choice- it’s either one portion or 1/2 a portion, and often the portion size is not defined. 
Also, the sleep recording is poor. If you sleep for a little bit, wake up, and then go back to sleep again after an hour or so, usually that is either not recorded or shown as one long sleep. And if you are recording manually, you’re not given any opportunity to record more than one “session” per calendar date. 
I’m finding that much of what is supposed to be automatically recorded is highly inaccurate, and there does not seem to be a way to correct it manually. So the summary reports are next to useless and don’t reflect what actually happened. 
Need options for far more details and choices!!!!

title: Inaccurate Fitness Stats
body:
I love the Galaxy Watch. However, the fitness stats from the Samsung Health app seem to be way way off. I have been wearing an Apple Watch, a Fitbit Charge 2, and my new Galaxy Watch together for several days. The Fitbit and Apple Watch report very similar steps, stairs, active minutes, sleep times, etc. The Galaxy Watch stats are always much lower (fewer steps, stairs, etc). I have tried wearing it tight, loose, in different places on my wrist — no difference. When I check on forums, this seems to be a VERY common problem. Samsung needs to get their act together. Why would you release an app without checking if it matches the stats being reported by competitors?? It is baffling.

If this is a software problem, get it fixed!

title: Review after one year
body:
This is a great app until you start using it.

Sync - in one word - nighmare. Everybody complains, but there is no development in this. You cant easyli sync data, especially historical data if you off for a few days. There is no push data button to send it all, you have to do tricks and hacks to keep sync alive, it updates usually what you dont need (stress ie) but no steps, floors.. why not to send it all in one package?

Friends - good to compete them, but only in steps?!? Why not to beat them in floors, sports (swimming, run, cycling)? To add a friend is sometimes run for a long distance.

Monthly challenges - still a lot users cheating with steps, no one cares. Useless and dissapointing to compete fake users who runs like Bolt even they sleeping.

Updates - in one year any significant updates to make the app better. Missing new ideas, tip and tricks to be more active.

Historical data - hard to get easy information about my progress, compare my KPIs, go thru journeys (ie with friends, family).

If this is a work of official support of Samsung.. its a crap :(

title: Einfach nur Fantastisch 😍
body:
Die bisher beste Fitness-App die ich je hatte!
Als erstes ist die Vielzahl von verschiedenen Fitness-Arten nicht zu übersehen. Man kann von Zirkeltraining über normale Liegestütz bis hin zu Cardiotraining auswählen! Diese Vielfalt trägt zu 2 Sternen bei. Die normalen, am meisten benutzten, Features sind Schrittzähler und-oder schlaf-Rhythmen. Dies beschafft den 3ten Stern!
Das aber, meiner Meinung nach, beste Feature, welches auch die beiden letzten Sterne beschafft, ist die Globale Herausforderung. Den Drang das Ziel zu erreichen, lässt einen den Fernseher ausschalten, aufstehen, sich anziehen und rausgehen um das Schritt-Ziel zu erreichen.
Am Ende freut man sich über das geschaffte und ist motiviert für mehr! 

Im Großen und Ganzen eine Fantastische Fitness-App die einen durch spielerische Art zum Bewegen motiviert.
Glückwunsch an das Entsteller-Team! 👍🏼😁

body:

title: Schlaf
body: Schlafdauer sollte einstellbar. / korrigierfähig sein, da oft  und sonst die Zeit im Bett/wachzeit mit erfasst wird. Das Programm sollte die falsch erfasste wachzeit rausberechnen und die Schlafphasen neu anhand der kürzeren schlafdauer ermitteln können. Das verfälscht sonst das Ergebnis  der Leichtschlafphase und die gesamte Statistik. Zudem fehlen mir die Regenerationparmeter. Diese lassen sich gut mit dem Ruhepuls und den Schlafphasen in einer Nacht ermitteln. Damit sollte es eine Benachrichtigungsfunktion bezüglich des Immunsystems/ Krankheiten auf der Grundlage des Ruhepuls in den  Schlafphasen über einen Zeitraum geben. Dazu gibt es auch einige Studien. Was auch fehlt, ist eine Schlafstörungerkennung. Dazu gibt es auch einige Studien. Diese Daten können anhand von Bewegungsdaten, auch wenn nur durch Handbewegungen möglich ist  und durch eine schnarcherkennung sowie eine Atemausetzer Erkennung erfasst werden können. Danke

title: Die Synchronisation ist eine Zumutung und Frechheit
body:
Entgegen der angegebenen Kompatibilität mit Apple Produkten funktioniert die Synchronisation leider nicht. Es ist reine Glücksache und funktioniert auch nur, wenn man App und Uhr ( in meinem Fall die Samsung Gear fit 2 pro) zurücksetzt und alles neu installiert. Damit sind allerdings alle gespeicherten Daten weg. Nach spätestens drei Tagen funktioniert die Synchronisation wieder nicht mehr. Gleiches gilt für die Galaxy Fit App, die man parallel installieren muss, damit die Uhr überhaupt erkannt wird. 
Das ganze ist eine Zumutung und eine Frechheit, dass an dieser überhaupt mit IOS-Kompatibilität geworben werden darf.

title: mit Gear Fit 2 Pro einfach nur Müll
body:
Die Synchronisation der Daten ist nur möglich, wenn die Gear frisch gestartet ist. Läuft sie schon etwas, dann fliegt beim Start der App die Bluetooth-Verbindung weg und man muss die Gear und die App neu starten. Wenn man nicht regelmäßig synchronisiert hat und es etwas mehr Daten sind, scheitert das Sync gerne mal und es wird scheinbar immer wieder versucht. Als Ergebnis ist der Akku der Gear dann in spätestens 8 Stunden leer.
Auch wenn man die App auf dem IPhone ohne Sync-Probleme nicht konsequent schließt geht das mächtig auf den Akku der Gear.
Mit aktuellen IOS bzw. mit meinem neuen IPhone X geht nichts mehr. Nach dem Rest der Gear (mit neuem Telefon verbinden) dauert es wenige Tage, bis die Bluetooth-Verbindung immer nur noch wenige Sekunden hält, auch wenn die App nicht genutzt wird. Nach Deinstallation der App geht wenigstens die Anruf- und Nachrichtensignalisierung wieder zuverlässig.

title: Schlecht ist untertrieben
body:
Inzwischen verbindet sich die Uhr gar nicht mehr, ich kann gar nicht mehr zählen wie oft ich die Uhr zurückgesetzt habe. Der Support kann auch nicht wirklich weiterhelfen. Apple kann eben nur mit Apple, das hätte ich ja wissen müssen.

Alte Bewertung:
Ich verwende die App zusammen mit meiner Galaxy Watch S3 frontier.
Die Synchronisation findet nicht automatisch statt. Nur beim öffnen der App und dann heißt es warten.
Die synchronisierten Daten sind nicht synchron.
Die von Handy und Uhr gleichzeitig erfassten Daten werden nicht wie behauptet identifiziert und Redundanzen aus der Gesamtschrittmenge herausgerechnet.
Kurz um: Die Daten sind nicht im Ansatz verwertbar und müllen nur den Speicher zu.
Darüber hinaus ist die Möglichkeit der Datenauswertung relativ begrenzt.
GPS oder Geschwindigkeitsdaten sind nur auswertbar, wenn ein workout explizit gestartet wird.
Mit Smart hat das nichts zu tun.
Absolut nicht empfehlenswert.
Weder die App noch die verfügbaren Wearables.

title: Das klappt nicht !!!
body:
Ich habe mir auf mein IPhone die Samsung Health App geladen um mit meiner Frau am Monatsbattle teilzunehmen. Meine Frau hat ein Samsung Handy und die Gear pro. 
Ich hatte Samsung auch bereits wegen meines Problemes angeschrieben. Zwei Wochen später keine Antwort. 
Meine Frau und ich laufen die gleiche Strecke und haben unterschiedliche Schrittzahlen. Hier ein Beispiel von gestern: meine Frau hatte 27000 Schritte, mir hat die App 18000 Schritte gut geschrieben. Das wiederholt sich an etlichen Tagen immer zwischen 3000 und 10000 Schritten weniger. Das passt nicht!!! Parallel läuft bei mir Stepz und die Apple Watch mit GPS mit. Da kommen annähernd die Selben Schrittzahlen raus wie bei meiner Frau. 
Das interessante ist, dass Samsung Health auch auf diese Daten Zugriff haben möchte und hat! Diese aber nicht nutzt. 
Fazit ich muss für die Strecke von 200000 Schritten ca. 40000 Schritte mehr machen als andere, die Samsung Geräte haben. Ein fairer Wettkampf. 
Da Samsung nicht mal in der Lage ist zu schreiben wir kümmern uns drum, kann diese Bewertung leider nur mit einem Stern ausfallen.

body:
Hi Samsung Team,

Die Galaxy Watch App scheint nun auch an Tag 2 zu funktionieren. Die Samsung Health App ist bereits wieder ausgestiegen. Echt frustrierend! Die Samsung Health App meldet „keine Wearables verbunden“. In den Einstellungen  sehe ich aber meine Galaxy Watch als registriertes Zubehör. Kontrolliere ich bei Bluetooth, sind beide Instanzen zur Uhr verbunden. Ich schaffe es nicht, dass die Galaxy Watch mit der HealthApp kommuniziert, sobald er Fehler einmal aufgetreten ist. Nur ein kompletter reset/Neuinstallation ermöglicht das Verbinden zur Samsung Health App. Die Uhr hat neueste Firmware, die Apps sind neu aus dem AppStore geladen. Die Installation erfolgte nach Vorschrift (Ich habe die Samsung Apps die Bluetooth Einstellungen vornehmen lassen). Galaxy Watch App scheint stabil, Samsung Health App steigt spätestens an Tag 3 aus. 

So darf das nicht sein! Bitte um Lösungen!

Ja und was ist passiert? Richtig! Samsun und Apple haben keinen Bock miteinander zu reden und die Daten werden nicht korrekt oder gar nicht übertragen. Wer von den beiden Schuld ist weiß ich nicht aber Dir App ist voll unbrauchbar. Der Account meldet dich ständig ab und Bluetooth geht nur bei jedem 3. Anlauf. Die App verfügt nur über rudimentäre Sportarten und ist nicht annähernd so komfortabel und erweiterbar wie ich das von Garmin gewohnt bin. Öl wenn man nichts anderes kennt ist das vielleicht ok aber schön ist anders

Das Programm ist somit nicht mehr nutzbar (startet nicht mehr, kann nur endlos auf Wiederholen klicken).

title: Keine Synchronisation der Schritte und Trainingsdaten
body:
Sehr Schade, endlich ist das Update für die S3 da und jetzt geht die Health App nicht ordentlich 😞
Update: Nach Update der App funktioniert Synchronisation der Pulsdaten. Die Synchronisation der Schritte funktioniert zwar aber die Zahl der Schritte in der App weicht von der Anzahl auf der S3 ab. Schlafdaten wurden heute gar nicht synchronisiert - klappt vlt ab morgen dann wieder. Ich hoffe es pendelt sich wieder ein und die Synchronisation funktioniert wie vor dem Update - insgesamt sieht das Update nämlich gut aus.
Ein zusätzliches Update nach Tizen 3.0 gibt es für meine S3 gerade nicht.
Update2: Die Anzahl der Schritte differiert nach Sync immer noch um 40-100 Schritte zwischen App und S3 (S3 als Schrittquelle). Das war vorher besser/genauer. Der Rest der App funktioniert nach Update. Deshalb jetzt 3 Sterne. Die anderen zwei gibt es wenn die App mit der App von meiner Frau (FitBit) mithalten kann 😊
Update3: Seit dem neusten Update der Gear geht gar kein Sync mehr. Die Hardware der Uhr ist super - die Software der Uhr ist OK - die Software für das Iphone ist unterirdisch. Ich hab die Uhr jetzt 6 Monate davon warte ich 80% der Zeit darauf, dass Samsung die Software wieder fixed 😡

Update 17.06.2018
Der Akku der Uhr hält nun nur noch 12Std. Ich kann nur jedem vor m Kauf dieser Uhr abraten der nicht Lust hat Samsungs Versuchskarnickel bzw. Betatester zu sein. Die Uhr habe ich jetzt fast ein Jahr und warte eig. nur auf Updates die die Uhr zum funktionieren bringen. Der Support vertröstet einen nur damit, dass man auf die evt. kommenden Updates warten soll. Schade um das eig. grundsätzlich gute Konzept.

title: Absoluter Mist!
body:
Man kann erst mal sagen: Alles was Samsung für die Gear S3 auf iOS abliefert, ist unbrauchbar. Nicht buggy, nicht verbesserungswürdig, sondern unbrauchbar!

Das geht mit der Companion-App los (Gear S), die mind. 2x pro Tag den automatischen Kontakt zur S3 verliert. Wobei man vorwegschicken muss, dass Tizen auf der S3 auch nur buggy ist - alles Zufall, mal gehts, mal nicht, Akkuverbrauch ist Zufall, vieles Wichtige ist nicht konfigurierbar (@Samsung: Schrittweite ist etwas individuelles, ebenso wie die Höhe von Stockwerken so rund um die Welt). Die ganze Uhr ist alpha bis beta, aber kein marktreifes Produkt. Habe sie auch einige Zeit mit einem Galaxy S7 verwendet, da wars gerade noch erträglich. Mit dem iPhone ist die S3 nun gänzlich unbenutzbar, bzw. sinnlos. Selbst wenn man alles reduziert und NUR Benachrichtigungen am Handgelenk erwartet - auch das geht nicht zuverlässig. Nützt dann freilich gar nichts.
Die Health App nun ist die logische Fortführung dieser programmtechnischen Katastrophe! Auch wenn das Gear Helferlein (Gear S) gerade mal mit der Uhr kommuniziert, die Health App synced trotzdem nichts. Auf der Uhr kann ich eine Woche Schlaf- und Bewegungsdaten abrufen (sind also definitiv da), Health tut auch für 1-3 Min. so, als würde es synchronisieren, allein am Ende landen keine Daten auf dem Handy. Eine Frechheit auch, dass man seine Daten zwingend bei Samsung abliefern muss. Samsung Account ist Pflicht! 

Wie gesagt, ich hatte die S3 vor dem iPhone, optisch wäre sie ein Highlight, aber mehr auch nicht. Seit Verwendung mit iOS stürzt die S3 übrigens auch 1x täglich mit verstümmeltem Screeninhalt ab, was die Uhr im Zweifel sogar als einfache Uhr disqualifiziert. Aus- und wieder einschalten und bis die Uhr dann wieder eine Zeit anzeigt, dauert Minuten - da ist jeder Termin verpasst.

Meine Empfehlung: Einfach nix von Samsung kaufen macht glücklich - ich werde es so tun!

UPDATE: Seit ich die obige Rezension geschrieben habe, 'terrorisiert' mich Samsung mit Mails! Der Inhalt: 
"Hi, Thanks for your feedback, we will pass your feedback to development team.“

Möchtest du deine Rezension bearbeiten?Du kannst auch den Entwickler kontaktieren.

Diese Mail bekomme ich seit 8 Tage jeden 2. Tag! BEIDE Links funktionieren übrigens nicht, was zwar nicht weiter stört, aber wieder mal die ganze Samsung-Qualität zeigt. Ich will aber weder den Entwickler kontaktieren (wozu? Steht alles in der Rezension) und erst recht will ich meine Rezension nicht ändern! Was soll die Frage überhaupt? Hört dann erst das Gespamme auf? Lachhaft! Nachdem die Mail aber so 'eintönig' ist, landet sie ab sofort in meinem Spamfilter - Gratulation Samsung, ihr habt nun eine eigene Spamregel bei mir.

title: Missing Functions
body:
In general Samsung Health is a good step, considering the compatibility of both brands.

Missing or suggestible functions are :

- integration of measured data by Samsung Gear into iOS Health

- customization of design/look of sleep and fitness analysis (Nowadays everything is about design and animation. It shouldn’t lights and movements everywhere but the current look is too „dry“. For example a bad sleep score should motivate the user for changes. Designs like apps e.g. “Sleepace” would be really great and interesting.

- The measured data should be able to be collected as a whole and extractable e.g. as .PDF or similar for personal uses

...

Summarizing everything, the app is really great but doesn’t use its whole potential.
But I’m excited about future steps and possibilities for new updates.
KEEP IT UP SAMSUNG!

Aber diese App in der die ganzen Daten zusammen laufen bringt mir rein gar nichts. Ich bin seit über 10 Jahren Apple Kunde. Habe dementsprechend viel in Apple Health an Daten. Sorry liebes Samsung Team .. Thema verfehlt. Man hat keinerlei Chance Daten in Garmin, Strava, Runtastic oder sogar ins Apple Health Center zu schicken.

title: Abandoned and Outdated on iOS
body:
I really love Samsung for its innovation and bold ideas. However, the Samsung Health project for iOS feels completely abandoned.

After so many years, there is still no proper integration with Apple Health, which is extremely disappointing. For an app in the health and fitness space, seamless data synchronization is essential. Without it, the user experience feels incomplete and fragmented.

It seems like all the company’s energy has gone into AI development, and unfortunately, this app has been left behind. It’s really sad to see such a promising product not receiving the attention and improvement it deserves ☹️

title: No funciona con IPhone S Max
body:
1ra Opinión: 
Imposible que cuente correctamente los pasos que están en el reloj !!. Tengo un iPhone s Max y la app no me cuenta dichos pasos, aunque si los del móvil aunque se desconecta todo el tiempo, al parecer la potencia del Bluetooth es muy débil. La sincronización entre Galaxy watch e IOS es deprimente en ese sentido !!. El reloj como tal es bonito más o menos igual en la calidad de los sensores que el APPLE watch lastima la compatibilidad entre ambos !!

2 da Opinión: 
Los de Samsung se han puesto en contacto conmigo a través de email, para enviarme un link en YouTube donde se Explica cómo seleccionar la fuente de pasos. Aún así mi aplicación Health no se actualiza con los pasos, de hecho no se actualiza desde hace dos Dias , a pesar de que la desinstalo y vuelvo a instalar, la app del Galaxy si reconoce al reloj y al móvil pero la app de Salud muestra sgte mensaje “ no hay ningún wareable conectado “ !!!. 

3ra Opinión : Sencillamente PENOSA la aplicación , una vergüenza para nada recomendable, no sincroniza nada con el S Max, además espero que me respondan lo antes posible y que no sea con otro link de YouTube !!!

title: Sync not working between Samsung Health and Gear S
body:
Managing workout items via Samsung Health app (iPhone6, iOS 11.3) will not make the changes appear at the Gear Sport workout selection. 

Example: At the Health app (ver 1.3.0.041) I manage workout items; hide hiking and add badminton. 

Result: At the Gear Sport workout view, hiking is still at the workout selection, but badminton is not.

Furthermore: 
Updating the version button is not working within the app nor at the Apple store. There is ver 1.4.0 available, but the app is not in update mode although I have older version.

Update on 15.4.2018 to the same topic.
Version update worked, I have now ver 1.4.0.039 installed.
Results: 
1) activity data between 11.4. and 15.4. not visible at the Health app.
2) managing workout items at the Health app > nothing happens at the Gear Sport.

I start to lose faith on Gear Sport. At least it is not suitable for someone who uses iPhone6 and wants to track workout sessions.

Big bugs still to be fixed!

title: Bug
body:
Bonjour L’application bug sur iPhone 12. DES écritures dépassent de l’écran  Merci de corriger s’il vous plaît

Mise à jour
Jai un iPhone 12 et la dernière version de l’app avec la dernière version de iOS. 
Dans l’app quand je consulte mes données de courses ou aliments par exemple les boutons PISTE TENDANCE ET RÉCOMPENSE en français bien sûr, sont « coupés » et on ne peut lire que la moitié des écritures. La coupure est en sens horizontale. La partie haute de l’écran affichant par exemple COURSE est bien trop épaisse et vient couvrir les onglets qui permettent de naviguer. 
Je peux faire des captures d’écran et vous les transmettre via e-mail. 
Merci. Cordialement

title: Très décu
body:
Très peu de mise à jour. L’ECG, la SpO2 et la pression artérielle ne seront a priori pas implantés sur iOs. Lorsque j’ai acheté ma Galaxy Watch 3, cela n’était indiqué nulle part. Depuis Février Samsung annonce que ces fonctions ne sont déployées que pour les téléphones Samsung...
Au delà de ça l’application est instable, ça se déconnecte tout le temps. Les mises à jour sont très rares et n’apportent rien. L’altimètre fonctionne quand il a le temps. Un bon conseil fuyez cette marque quand on est sur IOS... je regrette amèrement vu le prix de la montre... je suis partis de chez Apple à cause du design rectangulaire... Apple si tous lis, tu ferais beaucoup d’heureux avec un design rond. Beaucoup de gens sont partis chez Garmin pour cette raison ...

title: Application basique mais conviviale
body:
L'application est très simple d'utilisation, relativement bien pensée au niveau de l'ergonomie et s'interface parfaitement avec les Galaxy Watch (tout du moins, pour ma part, entre une Samsung Gear S3 Frontier et un iPhone 7)

Toutes les fonctions de bases sont présentes. De plus, le bilan de suivi nutritionnel intègre une très grande quantité de produits du commerce et peut être complété par l'utilisateur.

Bien évidemment, l'intégration est extrêmement limitée, et même inexistante, avec  d'autres applications de suivi physique ou sportif disponibles sur l'Apple Store et avec l'appli native "Santé" d'Apple.

La compatibilité avec des accessoires Bluetooth sport ou santé, autres que les Galaxy Watch, est limitée à deux marques marques de balances (Xiaomi et Polar) et rien d'autre !

title: Review of Step Count Accuracy in Samsung Health App
body:
Overall, Samsung Health is a very good app with many useful features. However, I have concerns about the accuracy of the step count rankings. Some users appear to record over 120,000 steps in a single day on a regular basis, which seems highly unrealistic.

These figures raise questions about the accuracy and fairness of the rankings. They can also be discouraging for people who are genuinely trying to stay active and improve their fitness, as it becomes difficult to compete with what appear to be inaccurate or inflated step counts.

I would encourage Samsung to review how steps are tracked and validated to ensure the leaderboard reflects genuine activity. This would help maintain user trust and provide fair motivation for everyone using the app.

title: It kind of does what it needs to do
body:
The user experience is not great. No auto-sync meaning that every time you open the app, the data is out of date and you need to pull down to refresh. That usually does not sync anything so you need to try again a few more times. Than finally you get your data into the app. Now you need to reload Together tab. Now that Together tab is reloaded, you need to go back to main tab to resync with your watch so that the info on your watch is up to date. Oh yeah and also if you do not do this several-minute-process every die, you will likely lose data from your watch. It will be on your watch but the app will be like “meh too old, I am not going to sync that”. Also, it is not possible to share your sleep or steps from your watch with any other applications. 

So overall, it is not like it does not work. It does when you are patient enough and remember to go through the process daily. I am glad that they at least brought the Together feature to iPhone users and that they are still improving the app. However, at the moment the user experience makes me want to hit myself with a chair out of frustration.

title: Suggestions
body:
Application shows summary information data (per month, week or day) for running, but it counts only full kilometers, not full distance. For instance, two running sessions, 7,60km and 7,80km are count in summary as 14,00km , instead of 15,30km.

Another question is if you can show data in summary area based on distance covered? Currently data on graph can be shown only with time spent on training sessions, but it woud be better if end users can choose in application what is most important to be shown as a summary: distance covered, time spent, or something else.

In addition, I didn’t succeed to send error report via application itself because it crashes or reports an error each time.

Each time when I try to send error report I receive message “Error occurred” in grey box on the bottom of a screen. When I try to attach image in error report application crashes immediately. It is not an network error, it is repeatable behaviour that completely disrupt error report sending functionality.

title: Not realistic
body:
How possible this

If you mean 1 lakh (100,000) steps in one day, the distance depends on your stride length.

On average:

* 1 step ≈ 0.75 to 0.80 metres
* 100,000 steps ≈ 75–80 km

A quick estimate:

* 100,000 × 0.75 m = 75,000 m = 75 km
* 100,000 × 0.80 m = 80,000 m = 80 km

So, 1 lakh steps is approximately 75–80 kilometres for most adults.

but for most people it is extremely difficult and not practical to do every day in 1L steps!!!!!
If 1L steps on everyday means 

* 100,000 steps ≈ 75–80 km of walking.
* At a normal walking speed of 5 km/h, it would take about 15–16 hours of continuous walking (not including breaks).

My opinion is

For general health, 7,000–10,000 steps per day is a realistic and beneficial target for many adults, though the ideal goal depends on your age, fitness level, and health.

title: Works great but doesn’t sync with Apple Health
body:
Everything is great about this app. Tracks steps, running, cycling and all other forms of fitness, however you have to turn the respective health feature on.. in order for the app to track it.

The only area of concern is that the tracks separate steps count apart from what I get on Apple health and on my iWatch. The data from apple health and iWatch is more accurate and doesn’t sync with the Samsung health app data count. In spite of you trying to manually sync it, there are discrepancies on every day count between the two systems. 

In addition, I can’t keep carrying the phone whenever I run or cycle, hence I wear a smart watch. You have to develop an app that tracks the fitness workout through the watch as well. If there is such an app function available for iPhone and iWatch users it makes sense to disregard the apple health data and go with Samsung health.

title: Praticamente inutile
body:
Son più le volte che non sincronizza (dicendo nessun dispositivo collegato) che quelle che lo fa.

Se anche riesce a sincronizzare (dopo tanti tentativi e accensioni e spegnimenti del BT) recupera i dati dell’ultima giornata ma nulla dei giorni precedenti, lasciando buchi di giorni o settimane nel trend.

In pratica, non conservando i dati, è come avere l’orologio (un galaxy watch ultimo modello) in stand alone.

Apple watch mi piace esteticamente meno, ma se si vogliono le funzioni di uno smart watch non è ancora possibile mescolare Samsung ad Apple (di chi sia la colpa non lo so, ma il risultato non cambia).

title: Non funziona
body:
Installata verso la metà di aprile, per le prime due settimane non l’ho usata molto ma non ho notato grandi malfunzionamenti.
Ora dice di essere sincronizzata con il Gear S, ma riporta dati completamente diversi e non carica gli allenamenti dei giorni precedenti, né considera i nuovi “record” raggiunti.
Banalmente, nemmeno il numero di passi registrato dall’app corrisponde a quello del Gear S, né selezionando “tutti i passi” si ha una stima verosimile.
Ho provato dall’app a selezionare Impostazioni-contattaci/segnala errore: mi fa allegare fotografie, mi fa scrivere, ma al momento di inviare dice che c’è stato un errore! Sto provando da due giorni ma la situazione non cambia.
La utilizzo su iPhone7 e ad oggi è totalmente inutile.

31.05.2018: Non funziona. Dati passi e salita completamente diversi da quelli registrati dal Gear. E la funzione per comunicarvi i malfunzionamenti...non funziona! Vorrei allegare fotografie ma non posso nemmeno qua.

Inutile

body: Galaxy Fitアプリではバンドと繋がっているにも関わらず、このアプリは頻繁に「バンドを検索中」となりデータ同期できなくなります。 Bluetoothを電源をオフ→オンすれば再度同期できるようになるのですが、切れてることひ気づかず過去のデータがバンドからも消えてしまうと、非同期のデータは失われます。 ちなみに、オフにしたタイミングでバンドは振動するので、iPhoneと繋がってることは確実です。アプリはほぼアップデートされないですし、アプリも遅く頻繁に落ちるので大変不満です。

title: Android版と比べて出来ることが減った
body:
先月、iPhone13miniに機種変更するまでの約5年、Androidでこのアプリを使っていました。
Android版は、ヘルスケアに関するたくさんの項目を１つのアプリで管理でき、さらにトレーニングもできるので、大変重宝していました。

　しかし、iOS版では、月経の管理機能や、ランニング中に１kmごとに音声で知らせてくれる機能などが無く、非常に不便を感じながら使っています。

普段は、通知音は不用ですがランニング(だけに限らずトレーニング)時やBluetoothイヤホンに接続している時などは、音声での通知ができるようにして欲しいです。

title: ソフトが悪いのか？
body:

頻繁にデータをスマホとやりとりするためか、電池の減りが早い気がします。
ソフトは少しづつ改善はしているが、その改善は遅い。ソフトは全体的にイマイチ。画面も見にくい。正直、評価1はつけ過ぎと思うが、最低レベルという意味で、1をつけました。
スマートバンド本体が壊れるまでは、使いますが、もう2度と買わないシステムと思う。

title: 염경중 중1일동
body: 안녕하세요 저희는 염경중 중1일동입니다 학교 수행평가 후기를 작성하려고합니다 체중감량, 근육 키우기, 밸런스 운동, 달리기 등등 다양한 운동을 측정할 수있어 좋았고, 하루에 걸음걸이를 알 수있는게 좋았습니다 그리고 요일별 기록도 챙겨볼 수있어서 어떤 요일에 활동량을 늘려야 할지 계획을 세우는데에도 도움이 되었습니다 하지만 폰이 삼성이지만 나이가 안돼 삼성계정이 없어서 들어갈 수없고, 처음부터 막혀 앱을 들어갈 수없어 불편했다 또는 갤럭시 워치가 없다면 심박수 측정이 불가능 하거나 보고싶지 않은 정보를 계속 보여준다 등 불편한점도 있었습니다 읽어주셔서 감사합니다 항상 좋은앱을 만들어 주셔서 감사합니다

title: 달리기 백그라운드 실행
body:
달리기를 하려고 할 때 앱 화면을 켜놓은 상태가 아니면 달리기가 측정되지 않습니다. (정확하게 말하자면 타이머는 작동하나 거리가 측정되지 않음)

이런 현상이 겨울에는 문제가 됩니다. 온도가 낮아서 배터리 전압이 빨리 떨어지기 때문에 화면을 켜놓은 상태에서 사용을 하면 전원이 금방 꺼질 수가 있습니다. 

달리기 시작 버튼을 누른 다음에 화면을 끄거나 백그라운드 상태로 돌려도 운동이 측정될 수 있도록 업데이트 부탁드립니다.

title: Accessory not found error
body:
1. 기존에 내 장치를 watch 앱과 health 앱에 성공적으로 연동해서 이주 잘 사용하고 있었다.
2. 내 장치와 watch 앱의 연결을 끊고 다시 연결했다. (이 과정에서 내 장치가 초기화되었다.)
3. 다음 작업으로 health 앱과 내 장치를 연동을 하려했지만, 내 장치를 찾을 수 없다는 메세지만 출력된다.
4. health 앱 재설치해보기도 하고, 내 시계를 재시작 해보기도 하는 등 모든 노력을 했으나 health 앱은 여전히 내 장치를 찾지 못하고 있다.
5. 반면, health 앱에 등록된 액세서리 목록을 보면 내 장치가 등록되어 있다고 나온다. (하지만 실제로 동기화는 안되고 있음)

title: 아이폰용은 아직 오류가 많습니다.
body:
1. 1일 칼로리 소모량 오류 (21837562 이런 식으로 이상하게 집계)
2. 칼로리 섭취량 워치에 중복 집계 오류 (삼성헬스에서 지워도 워치에서는 그냥 기존 것과 합산됩니다.)
3. 내음식 삭제 불가 (등록 후 아직 삭제 불가합니다.)
4. 주변기기 연동이 잘 안됩니다. (미스케일이 연동된다고 나오는데 실제로 체중 측정된 것이 연동이 안됩니다.)
5. 내음식에 기반해서 아침 식사 입력 후 세부내용 (ex. 밥 한공기 —> 반공기)을 수정하면 칼로리 집계 오류납니다. 뭔지 잘 모르겠음.
6. 영양정보 입력하는 부분이 부실합니다. (비타민 d 뭐 이런 거 입력이 아예 안되네요)

이미 한 달 정도 전에 위의 오류 중 일부는 삼성헬스에 문의한 적도 있으나, 고쳐줄 생각이 없는 것 같습니다. 그냥 개발팀에 오류를 전해 주었다 정도의 답변만 오네요.. 그럼에도 불구하고 잘 사용하고 있어.. 별 하나 더 드립니다. YAZIO 등은 유료라....; 아이폰 사용자지만 삼성도 잘됐으면 좋겠습니다.. 빨리 고쳐주세요.

답변의 성의가... 이미 그렇게 app.을 통해 요청했는데도 안되고 있다는 겁니다...

title: iOS and Samsung Galaxywatch problem
body:
So Im having trouble with Samsung health app on iOS system. I have iPhone 7 Plus with iOS 13.3.1 and Samsung Galaxy 46mm watch with  Tizen version 4.0.0.7 and all last system updates. The Phone and Watch connects trough bluetooth and shows up in settings, and also the Galaxy Watch app syncs, but Samsung Health can’t sync properly.
I checked all settings as app developer recomends, but nothing helps. 
I read that other users have same problem, and there was a solution but the solution works only once, if I want to check the data again, I need to restart the phone and watch again, which really is annoying.
I discovered, that one of the solutions, that helps sync is shortly switch off and on bluetooth on iPhone. But it is only a temporary solution. 
Also lately Ive noticed that something is using more watch batery than it should. When I bought it lasted 4days with a charge, but now it barely lasts for 2days with single charging. GPS and WI-FI I switched on for short time, only when I try to sync or when I do my workout. Screen brightness is set to minimum. NFC is off. 
My problems started when I reset my watch to factory settings. Whatch was asking for system updates. So I was forced to update it from Tizen version 4.0.0.4 to 4.0.0.7.  And thats when the watch started to misbehave. 
My son has same model phone and watch with same settings. On Tizen vers 4.0.0.4 he hasn’t got any problems as I did before updates. His watch lasts twice longer with same charging. 
Can I get a fix for this in nearest time, or it’s not worth it and users should just switch to other smartwatches?

title: IOS + samsung watch
body:
Samsung watch app works great. Samsung health app doesnt fully sync data with watch until you restart that watch. It will sync all data for few hours and then it will say that no device connected to app. But samsung watch works fine meanwhile with my watch device. It’s frustrating that I need to restart watch every 2-3 hours to get data synced with Health app. This app feels like beta version. And backup & restore function - what is that? It only backups weather forecast and notifications :D who neeed that? Why doesnt it backup my fitness data and settings? Last night in global steps challenge I had 191 000 steps. I deleted Health app from my phone and installed back because my watch couldnt sync with this app. After reinstall I lost all steps data. Somehow now i have only 101 000 steps in global challenge. I have no records of my workouts - nothing. Meanwhile in my watch I can see everything. So backup doesnt work, sync struggles to work. It’s quite bad :( 
Why cant watch and this app sync in the way that both devices shows the same information? If I have worked out past few weeks then why cant Health app download that data from watch device?

How Samsung imagines stealing Apple users if they provide product that bad?

Still the same problem after all updates. Does Samsung even cares?

3rd edit

I already sent error reports and debug data from watch and health app to Samsung help center. I recorded video and screenshots. Samsung help already has all that information. Still - it’s more than 1 month and nothing has changed.
No wait - after last firmware update my watch is using 2-3% battery in hour when idle. Before update I could get 4-5 days battery time. Right now it’s less than 2 days. Samsung watch app shows that Health app is using battery the most. But health app isn’t working properly. What else can I do? 
Factory resets and app reinstalls are done already

title: Beoordeling
body:
Goede morgen Samsung,

Situatie: iPhone 12 pro telefoon en een
                 Galaxy Watch 3 horloge en een      iWatch 4 om m’n andere pols omdat de Galaxy Watch 3 bij mij geen val detectie heeft, geen SOS knop, geen ECG kan draaien, dus moet ik de iWatch 4 er wel bij houden voor mijn eigen veiligheid. Ik ben hartpatiënt, vandaar. 

Geen dark stand. 
Kan hartslag grafiek niet vergroten en in mis een grit en de waardes in de grafiek. Kijk naar Fitbit. 
Geen zuurstof meting. 

Wat ook vervelend is dat ik vaak de Galaxy Watch 3 weer opnieuw moet zoeken. Dan zijn ze, de watch en de iPhone, elkaar weer kwijt. Nou weet ik wel dat een iPhone geen Samsung is, maar toch vind ik dat het wel stabieler hoort te zijn. 

Ik zou graag zien dat de app meer uitbreiding krijgt voor hart patiënten 
En dat ik mijn iWatch af kan doen omdat twee horloges dragen vervelend is en omdat de iWatch gewoon een lelijk ding is vergeleken met de Galaxy Watch 3, dat is echt een mooie smart watch. 

Verder ben ik dik tevreden hoor, dank dat ik mijn verhaaltje kwijt kon. 

Fijne dag verder

Met vriendelijke groeten

Bronger Niehoff
te Delfzijl

title: Samsung Health and Samsung Galaxy watch active
body:
The Bluetooth connection is a bit off. The watch looses contact with the phone, even though they are in the same room, and even close together. 
All sync issues have been solved due to hardware problems. 

Problem solved! 18/06
Replaced my watch and the new one workes perfect! 

Jeg laster ned og installerer slik videoene viser, men den S health vil ikke koble til min klokke. Jeg får beskjed om at «ingen kroppsnære enheter er koblet til»

Den registrerer ikke puls, eller søvn. Det eneste som registreres er aktivitet, men det tror jeg det er telefonen som har registrert.

Update: 
Den har plutselig begynt å ta inn data fra klokken, den syncer fortsatt ikke søvn.

Update 15/06:
I did both steps, and it worked. 
But then it stopped syncing. I tried syncing again and repeated both steps this morning still no wearable device. Then when hiking in the woods i tried again, and it suddenly did. 
So I tried again later, and it wouldn’t. Even disconnected WiFi from both devices(as in the woods), didn’t work. Is it really supposed to be this unstable?

Update 17/06

Nothing I’ve tried works. Beginning to think that there’s something wrong with the Bluetooth signal. The watch is receiving notifications but it has difficulties sending information to the app. Am taking the watch back tomorrow to see if they maybe can replace it, if they can’t figure it out.

title: Horrendous
body:
Not worth the money. 
If you need this app to connect with your Samsung watch good luck. 

I hope my issue is with the watch rather than the app but the watch requires this app and it really does not work. I have a Samsung Gear Fit 2 Pro and the sequence required to sync involves three apps and must be done in the correct order. Most days I have to restart both phone and watch and despite showing as connected in a couple of places (Bluetooth settings and Samsung Gear app) most days this app says there are no wearable devices connected. So I can rarely download data and when it does work I get two days max of data losing the rest. It’s a celebration when it does download. 

I’ve contacted the support team and the response is slow, and really demonstrated that the developer needs to rethink the experience for users - eg the need to open the Samsung Gear app and then the Samsung Health app (but not by using the Samsung Health icon in the Gear app as that doesn’t work). 

I won’t start on the watch that is a whole other basket case of issues definitely no good if you want reliable GPS or sleep data. It’s so wrong it is laughable. 150 kilometers in 20 minutes of exercise?

title: Beznadzieja
body:

Po co funkcja zliczania wypitej wody? Aplikacja powinna podpowiadać ile wody pic / dzień i przypominać o piciu. Wówczas mógłbym oznaczać ile wypiłem. W ten sposób widziałbym ile jeszcze wody powinienem wypić. Ilość powinna być korygowana o temperatur otoczenia i latem narzucać większe ilości żeby pic. Aplikacja niestety nic nie przypomniana, a notować to ja mogę na kartce lub w excelu.  

To samo z kaloriami. Skoro ktoś chce liczyć kalorie i zdrowo się odżywiać to aplikacja mogłaby przypominać co np 3h zjedz coś, zjedz owoc, wypij wodę, itp.

title: Samsung Gear 3
body:
Покупал эти часы в 2017 г. 
Это был мой первый девайс с определением моей активности на руке. Честно говоря носив его, я не ценил, и не осознавал полезности его функционала. В 2022 году они перестали держать заряд. И я одел стрелочные часы. Оооо и тут я понял как мне их не хватает. У меня как будто выключили свет. Я не знал какая у меня активность в течении дня. Как я спал. Крч, всё познаётся в сравнении. И так, решил приобрести Хонор. Почитал немного отзывов, посмотрев обзоры. Купил. Проносив хоноры первый месяц, я понял как они врут, к примеру в полдень я уже достигал пика активности выполнял все поставленные цели. Пульс измеряется на них с большим опозданием. Нажав измерить пульс они не покажут тебе в этот момент какой у тебя пульс. А выведут показания в течении 20 минут. Ну вообщем на этом моя с ними дружба закончилась. Купил опять я Samsung и не на радуюсь.

title: The 1.14.7 update causes the app to quit in background while tracking exercise.
body: I used to track my indoors exercise bicycle and watch YouTube at the same time. It worked like magic while you didn’t touch the app for the past 2 years of no updates. Now you destroyed my day to day workflow with the most recent 1.14.7 update – the app quits randomly in the background and the ongoing exercise record is gone forever upon relaunching the app. My Galaxy Fit2 stops tracking my heart rate as well. In 1.14.6 and earlier, the iPhone’s clock turned blue as if Samsung Health was Google Maps during navigation. I suppose it was done to prevent the app being unloaded from the memory. Now it does not do that and I can not track my daily exercise anymore. This is the 5th time this has happened to me this week, and I see no reason to keep using the band and it’s corresponding software anymore.  Judging by your previous updates’ release dates I assume you will fix this in two years time, if ever. Just like you ruined notifications on Galaxy Fit2 around Christmas 2022 and you are yet to release a patch. I’ve been waiting for 2 years now, I feel like I’m being treated as a money bag rather than a client at this point. I regret investing so much into the Samsung ecosystem and I’m looking forward to stop using your software and corresponding hardware completely, since you keep releasing great products and keep ruining them with your useless updates cleverly disguised as “bug fixes” so that we buy your newer stuff that costs an arm and a leg to buy.

title: Это тамагочи, а не часы
body:
Ответ на рекомендации:соединение забывал.  толку никакого. Соединение часов с телефоном живёт своей жизнью. Приложение в ФОНЕ НЕ РАБОТАЕТ.  СО СТАНДАРТНЫМ ПРИЛОЖЕНИЕМ IOS ЗДОРОВЬЕ НЕ СИНХРОНИЗИРУЕТСЯ  всё остальное без изменений.  Теперь считанные данные не сохраняются в программе.  Собрать статистику не возможно.  Часы автоматом не подключаются.  То есть это зависит от фазы Луны на Плутоне.  Хочу подключусь, хочу нет. Приложение в бекграунде не работает. За 500 евро тамагочи, которое нужно холить и лелеять. Это ни разу не бизнес помощник.  Это выброшенные деньги.  За два года использования часов, окончательно понял, что Самсунг НЕ УМЕЕТ ДЕЛАТЬ ЗАКОНЧЕННЫЕ УСТРОЙСТВА.  Только комплектующие.  Больше никогда сам не куплю готовое устройство. Все последние обновления установлены.  И на часы и на iPhone 11.

title: Хорошо
body:
Пожалуй лучшее приложение. После того, как заменил браслет Самсунг (не смотря на заявленную водонепроницаемость - купание в Охотское море их отправило на тот свет),  на часы от Аппл, столкнулся с проблемой: стандартное приложение здоровье не дотягивает по функционалы до этого, или очень запутанное («вы ходили вчера больше чем позавчера» - зачем эта инфа мне? Это мусор!). Считать калории, контролировать сон, учитывать вес, пульс и тп - нужно найти другие приложения, которые или с урезанным функционалом, или с рекламой, но все требуют плату за кучу ненужной информации и сомнительных измерений.
Подкосу снова поставил это приложение. Жаль что не работает так плотно с часами от Аппл как с  браслетками и часами от Самсунг. Но всё равно: 5 звёзд!

title: Нет синхронизации со strava, garmin и т.д. Само приложение очень урезанное
body:
1. Нет синхронизации с другими фитнес помощниками  ( strava, garmin, etc. )Это существенный минус.
2. Нет возможности экспортировать данные о тренировке в файл , что бы потом загрузить в другие аналитические системы. 
3. В самом приложении нет никакой аналитики тренировки. Не возможно посмотреть на каком участке пробежки/похода/велотрека какие показатели скорости и пульса. Просто одна картинка с графиком, которая не масштабируется и   не накладывается на геотрек. 
4. Нет WebUI, как у strava или garmin. 

Пользуюсь совместно с часми galaxy watch , данные синхронизируется, но в приложении от них очень мало толка. Раз вы отменили возможность синхронизации со strava, хотя бы сделайте возможность экспортировать данные , в месте с геолокацией в файл.

title: Makes me frustrated over meaningless things
body:
The application logs me out quite often, and it’s a little annoying to constantly log in, even though there’s nothing that could cause this in the settings. 

But the Together function makes me actually stressed. If I can’t see when the stars in the challenges expire, I can’t plan gathering them. I don’t want to make an extra effort within last 36 hours. I want to plan a gradual progress day by day. Besides, in my opinion, it’s not fair that your steps in the challenge only are counted from the moment of registration in the challenge. 

I understand that it’s done for engagement and retention, but it just makes me frustrated and stressed. I deleted the application, don’t want to be manipulated into stress.

title: App iis great - Samsung Watch not so  great
body:
I love the Samsung Health app on my iPhone 7. It tracks everything I want, diet, training. The interface is intuitive. One feature I would like is the abaility to edit the exercises on mthe app and on my watch, removing the ones i never uee. It would also be nice if I could track other exercises. That sadi, the fatal flaw is the watch, mine is a Samsung Active 2. It fails regularly, every few months like clockwork. The backup funnction does not back up all the training data so that means, every few months I just have to reset the watch and lose all that data.The app says you an download your data but Iäm here to tell you thatäs nonsense. You can’t. The downloaded file is a locked zip file and you cannot restore from it so it’s useless. The net result is that there is no point tracking my fitness data with the Samsung watch. Samsung says I should send the watch in for service. From what I see on Amazon and elsewhere, the issues I have with the Samsung watch are all too common. The watch is buggy.. If Samsung is offering to fix it free of charge, I would welcome that. Otherwise I\m not investing another cent in Samsung products. I\m going to get an Apple watch. Friends tell me they are worth the extra money because they just work.

UPDATE 
I’ve gotten myself an Apple watch and life is much better.  It just works so much better than Samsung with an iPhone .  I’m still using the Samsung Health iPhone app, looking for a replacement 

My advice for iPhone users:   Get an Apple watch and find a different health app, one that backs up your data and allows you to download your data.  This one does not.

title: Great potential, but lacks basic Apple Health-integration
body: This app could have been so much better if it wasn’t locked down to a one way synchronization of steps, namely only to Samsung Health. As a user of an iOS device, I would expect an application which is integrated with a premium smart watch as the Galaxy Watch Active 2, to provide the most basic parameters of step and distance synchronization back to Apple Health. Lacking this basic basic feature, along with other parameters such as pulse, sleep, water, nutrients, oxygen, etc, makes the advanced Samsung Galaxy Watch and Samsung Health features unavailable on iOS. Having used the Watch and health-app from Samsung on a Samsung device, there is so much more to make available for an iOS user. Please consider activating these additional features as Apple health already is available.

title: Terrible
body:
To synchronize your Galaxy Watch, you need two apps and you need to synchronize manually. The latter is no biggie per se but everytime the app is updated you’re in for a surprise: If you forget to synchronize for some time, all your not yet synchronized data is gone. I’ve lost data for many days like this, several times. Sometimes you even have to completely reset and re-pair your watch to get it to synchronize again. Loosing all data and settings, of course.

The app is also lacking basic functionality; e.g. it doesn't show GPS tracks, something you’d simply expect from a fitness app in 2020 as the watch does have and use GPS, but probably only for calculatimg distance and speed.

title: Account Reset
body:
The app is great and it is a lot of fun to compeat against my parents, but now, for the third time, my account has been reset! I still have my old profile picture and friends but all of my step tracker history is removed! I had completed a lot of global challenges and I had lots of badges, and this is the third time everything disappears! 
When I open the app sometimes it looks like I’m opening it for the first time! I press login and gets tossed into the app and everything is gone. 
Since it has happened three times now, I hope you guys will fix it! 

7/11 2019:
I had a look at the website you linked but did not find anything useful. After reinstalling the app it worked for a few weeks, but today when I went to my account all of my progress both in all the global challenges I had completed, all of my rewards, all of my step tracker history, EVERYTHING was gone. Again.    
I understand that this is a problem that probably not many people have, making it a hard issue to solve. This is not meant as any offense towards the app, I still love it and it’s developers, it’s just frustrating having to start all over again.
I believe in you guys!

title: It’s an ok app
body: Overall I like the look and feel of the Samsung health app. It seems to have some of the stuff I need. I’m transitioning over from Fitbit so there are some features I am hoping Samsung can try to adopt. For instance, this app needs a calorie function similar to Fitbit. Fitbit shows calorie intake and calories burned and they calculate for you weather or not you have burned enough calories to stay in a certain range. To me that is a great incentive to be a little more active when I can see if I have burned enough calories to have a snack and still maintain a caloric deficit. And it isn’t just as simple as setting a calorie intake goal for the day. If I tell Fitbit I want to stay 200 intake calories below my calories burned it just adjusts throughout the day. If I have been more active it allows me to consume more. Also Fitbit has a very nice UPC (barcode) scanner option for when you are logging what you are eating. I have not found that in the Samsung Health app. Lastly I would like to have the ability to customize the three main focus points on the Home Screen. I am not interested in my sleep patterns so I would much rather replace that with a calories burned tile.

This app was recently upgraded, and ever since, the app has lost a lot of functionality for food logging. Number one, on the meal screen, it won’t let me scroll down to see all the snack meal categories, so I can’t use 2 out of 6. It’s a minor inconvenience but I liked how granular it was with tracking. I am on a 15 Pro, and I’ve attempted app closures, phone restarts, and even a fresh app install, and still no fix.

Number two, you can no longer add custom food items with macros, so no creating “favorite meals” out of your custom recipes to track, you have to search for each item individually, adjust serving sizes, etc, it’s a pain. It’s a shame that this app lost that feature, because I find this app easier to use than MyFitnessPal, and the custom macro feature on that app is present but is behind a paywall.

title: Lacks integration with iOS
body:
I’ve used the Android version for years and really liked it and served as a one-stop-shop for health and fitness tracking.  Unfortunately the iOS version is extremely limited in that unlike other iOS apps, Samsung Health does not allow the data it collects (e.g. from my Galaxy Watch 3) to be shared with other iOS apps (specially Health).  It is also unable to pull in data from other iOS apps except for some very basic data (step count and walk/run distance).  This prevents it from being the ‘Hub’ that the Android app is and significantly limits the value of it.  Want to track calories? Scale weight? Track non running workout activities?  Nope… not if you want a comprehensive summary and analytics.

This lack of data sharing integration is too bad as I really like my Galaxy Watch 3 and find it superior to iWatch in many ways.

title: Poor cross platform support
body:
Some friends have Androids, some have iPhones. A bunch of them were already using Samsung Health, so we wanted to see if we could integrate and compete on steps during the week. Unfortunately iPhone users are not allowed to join step challenges with android users. Okay, fine.

But then we realized you can add friends to your leaderboard, regardless of platform, which is a huge win. Now though we can't do challenges together, we can use the leaderboard to informally compete over the 7 day rolling week. We are all fine with this.

Except we just realized for the iPhone folks, Samsung Health ONLY pulls steps from the iPhone itself as the data source, meaning that Apple Watch steps are not tracked at all. Despite the fact that I even disabled step tracking on the phone itself, and prioritized the Apple Watch in Apple Health as the #1 data source for step tracking, Samsung Health will not pull any steps at all unless they are from the iPhone. (None of us have Samsung watches)

This is a huge missed opportunity. If it's pulling data from Apple Health anyway, why can't it pull from different data sources? It's all in Apple Health already.

Once again, we are kind of back to square one on this.

title: Lacking needed Health integration
body:
This app works as it should in all regards, except in one very important way: it does not write any data to the iPhone’s Health app.
This makes integration with all other apps impossible. As a personal example, I cannot sync my steps from my Samsung Gear S3 watch to MyFitnessPal because Samsung Health doesn’t write my step count to my phone’s step data. I can see my steps in the Samsung Health app, but this information remains useless to all outside apps (such as MyFitnessPal, which is a big part of my health management as a formerly obese person trying to stay in shape).
I may not be on Android, but I’m still using a Samsung watch and a Samsung app, yet I’m being neglected as a customer and pushed toward getting an Apple Watch simply because I made the switch from a Galaxy to an iPhone.

2nd UPDATE I response to developer’s reply: I’ve already followed the procedures you lay out to remove, reset, and then reinstall on both my phone and watch.

I wish the developer would rewrite the app so that Samsung Health would be able to receive the watch information, whether through the Galaxy Watch app or (better yet) directly.

title: Absolutely love my Gear Fit2 Pro & this app but have questions
body:
**UPDATED**
My husband bought me the watch a few years ago.  In over 30 years of marriage definitely one of his best choices!  At that time I used the Android app on my LG K20 VS501; despite what many have reported I never experienced any problems even while using Bluetooth headphones.
The Android app allowed me to access music from my phone directly from the app while using the exercise tab for tracking walking.  Additionally, I was able to receive distance, speed, pace etc. cues audibly which I could set through my settings.  That feature was a big help!
Fast forward:  last summer I moved into the iPhone XR.  I set everything up with the Apple apps.  Connects easily every time, & this app also allows for easy syncing.  At first I drove myself crazy trying to find my 2 favorite features:  the music icon & audible cues.  At first I thought the cues were just not coming through my headset but after trying it without headphones I discovered there were none, only countdown.  (Countdown also does not come through Bluetooth headset.). I even switched to the running tab, thinking the option would be there; nothing.  Yes, I tried without music:  no more nice fellow voice to encourage me.
Although the missing link to my music can be worked around I really miss the audible cues.  Am I missing something as to how to find such setup ( which was easy in Android)?  Is there a reason why those features are not in the app for Apple?
**Finally, one additional question:  although I have my step count set to be from my watch exclusively with the app (all shows correctly!) since my phone is not tied to my hip the integration with Apple’s Health app only shows my phone’s step count.  Why does the app’s step count not utilize my choice of source when combined with the health app?  I use the Health app to integrate with rewards for healthy living from Walgreens & AARP.
Thank you!

***Nice quick response***
It is a rare instance where a developer offers a response so quickly!  Thank You!
Just to clarify, I already have my step count source set to my Gear Fit2 Pro.  (For anyone working off reviews, the developer’s response is an excellent demonstration how to do such if you do not know how to select!)
My steps always record from my watch, syncing each time I open my SHealth app.  My daily goal is always in my view, one way or another.
I guess what I am asking is, although my watch step count is correct in the SHealth app, why does my Apple Health app only show my phone’s step count (as opposed to my selected step count source properly recorded)?  Yes, they are linked with SHealth being a data source allowing Apple Health to read.  I have tried entering the difference in steps manually but it never saves. 
Thank you, again! 
STAY SAFE EVERYONE & PLEASE keep Social Distancing!

title: Disappointed
body: I think these are the best looking and highest quality smart watches on the market, however I am very unimpressed with the functionality. They are more concerned with the watch faces and looks than what the watch actually does. I chose this device because I wanted to track my steps, flights of stairs and sleep patterns. Since all other ones have less battery life and don’t look nearly as nice or are built as well, I picked the Samsung Frontier. It is incredibly accurate when it comes to steps, however the flights of stairs go off a 10 foot rise. Most household flights of stairs in America are only eight feet. I have tested this numerous times and only get zeros or ones regularly even by going up and down consecutively. The sleep piece is fair, same with the heart rate monitor and weather app. None of these communicate to your phone effectively at all. I have been playing with the settings for the last four months and can’t seem to get these to work the way the average person wants to use this device. NOTE: I am using an iPhone but I don’t think a android will be much different, just more apps. It is a beautiful WATCH though.

title: Good with iPhone 7, crap with iPhone 11
body:
I have a Samsung Fit, and this app plus the Galaxy Fit app worked fine (it’s an odd back and forth handoff, but it worked fine). Since I upgraded to an iPhone 11 about three weeks ago, the software is constantly losing the connection, the band resets randomly, my heart rate data only downloads once in a while, and none of my sleep data is being downloaded. When I got this, I just wanted a reliable heart rate and workout monitor, and the sleep tracking was a nice bonus. Now, I get consistent step data, occasional heart rate data, and no sleep data. The extremely annoying thing is that I can see a tiny chart of my sleep data on the Fit, and the app tells me it’s downloading the sleep data, but it never displays it. 
I don’t know if it’s an issue with the app on the new phone, or they just pushed a crap update about the same time I got it, but I’m extremely disappointed to find that a great, minimalist fitness tracker that met my needs has all but crapped out on me. 
I have a lot of Samsung products, but I won’t touch their phones or any of their other personal electronics, if they don’t fix this.

title: Completely useless - does not sync, wrong stats
body:
I really tried to like the Samsung Galaxy Watch and this app as I couldn't believe that I wasted $400 after so much research.

This watch, health app and Samsung service are all just plain terrible. Major issues:
- The samsung support team told me that samsung smart watches are not compatible with iPhones.
- The health app does not sync with iPhone unless you open the app explicitly, this means that all your weekly stats and everything that the watch records is lost within 3 days.
- It does not sync data with iPhone health app, so no other information from the health app gets transferred to samsung health and vice versa. This means that the smart scale that I have is useless alongside Samsung watch and the data recorded using other devices will never be seen alongside the samsung data.
- The app keeps logging me out every few days, which is super annoying.
- The swim tracking in the latest update to the galaxy watch does not work anymore, so the most important feature of the galaxy watch is gone now.
- Steps tracker counts the steps twice in the latest update and all the stats there are messed up.
- Sleep tracking has an error of +/-1 hour to start tracking, which is basically an error of more than 15% of the actual time sleep time for me.
- Samsung support is useless and is set up to pass the time so that your warranty is over. The only thing they kept telling me was that you should reset your watch, reinstall the apps and everything will work fine. I have done that thrice now. In the end they told me that Samsung watches are not compatible with iPhones.
- I upgraded from iPhone 6S as instructed by the Samsung support team and the issues persisted. Waste of more money!!

There are a lot of other issues as well but I think above are enough for you to stay away from Samsung on iPhones.

title: Samsung Health paired with iPhone XR
body:
In the two weeks I’ve had the Galaxy Active watch paired to my IOS Samsung Health, it has missed or does not automatically record about 1/3 of my activity and sleep. I thought it would pick up my exercise types as advertised. It has NOT recorded my tennis or swim routines this past week automatically. When I told the app I was initiating a tennis and swim workout it did record but only gave duration and calories burned. I was expecting more information given the specific selectivity of the excessive event. I did get some initial swim stats like SWOF in 1 of my three swim routines the past week. I also was not getting the heart rate tracking for each of the workouts, which should available. Regarding the steps, the watch records my steps bite the app does not / has accurately record them. For example my watch tells me I have walked 6700 steps this Thursday but the app only recorded 3400, really weird. The has inaccurately recorded my steps (watch different from app) for the past few day. It does not also sync consistently or when i open the Samsung watch app. Regarding the sleep tracker, this has not worked either. The first 4 days, ir was tracking my sleep with great stats, but now it does not record my sleep at all, I’ve had to manually put in my sleep. And when you do that it does give you the comprehensive sleep stats. 

I was excited and got the Samsung Active and Health app because I wanted to upgrade, better track and obtain more stats on my fitness routines and sleep. I am not sure what the issues are, but the combination of the Galaxy Active, Samsung Watch app for IOS and the Samsung Health app for IOS has failed me and I may go back to my faithful rock solid Garmin VivoFit.

title: Best health & activity tracking app
body:
I switched from Samsung galaxy s7 to iPhone X max (definitely will go back to Samsung again phone). This app is SO much better than apple’s health and activity apps and all other free of charge 3rd party apps in apple store. Why? All activity stats in 1 place and easily presented and working smoothly. Too bad Apple Watch doesn’t track sleep like Samsung watch gear sport (much better than I watch 3 in my opinion after using both).

Major pluses:
1) organization of the app and it’s free. The app includes sleep tracker, heart rate monitor, types of physical activities, etc. 
2) if u have Samsung watch, u score with this app. It works excellently with Samsung watch and transfers data. U can download Samsung watch app in apple store.
3) if u have no watch, u can select activity (running, walking or HIIT or barre) and turn it on to start tracking and then manually stop to get the stats. U won’t get heart rate measure unless u have watch or Samsung phone with the finger heart rate sensor. 
4) in case of Apple Watch, u can allow access for this app to get from apple’s health and activity apps (very annoying AND redundant that u have to look at both apps with terrible layout to see your data. 
5) app data presentation. I love how when u run/walk and click on the app and it shows u your route on the map, distance, time ran, calories burnt, heart rate and max heart rate (if u have watch and/or Samsung phone), steps and chart for all this. Then it tells u how it compares to your previous days (it’s duper nice how u see and switch between day and monthly activity) and to other people who use this app for your age, sex, fitness level, etc.

title: Needs work.
body:

How about the watch dying in under 8 hours if I leave the Bluetooth connection on (using it as a smart watch instead of a regular watch?) Bluetooth off yields like a week of battery life. What is going on here?

What about phantom alarms that just go off at 4 am and there is no way to delete them?

I want the watch to work, and I want the phone app to work, and I don’t want to have to “reset the watch” or “reinstall the app” because my expectation is for the thing to actually work. As a watch—as a fitness and sleep tracker—not as a $250 wrist-mounted dead battery. I cannot rely on this. What is the point of a broken watch?

I have the latest firmware.

title: Much improved, but still buggy
body:
The app largely does what you want from a health tracker, though the interface isn't entirely intuitive. You can view and enter data from selecting in the goals display or by clicking on a tracker item added to the grid. What I don't understand is why those take you to different interfaces for the same data. It's like the developers couldn't decide on an approach so they gave us both, but both are incomplete without the other view.

Syncing is much improved with the latest version of the software, plus a firmware update on my G3 watch. Biggest problem for me is a date/time bug which affects entering "dinner" details. Looks like it doesn't correctly account for your local timezone (I'm on EDT) so entries will disappear for today and show up instead for tomorrow. Sometimes it doesn't happen immediately, so you briefly see the totals you expect only to have them change. Super frustrating as it seems there's no good way for the user to correct it and force the date, and you can't delete the data for tomorrow until, well tomorrow. I've even seen it happen trying to correct data for the previous day despite having the date and time explicitly set.

title: Great and useful app
body:

While I don’t think that the app does 100% of the same things that the Android app can do, it is really close (and improving). This is one of the best cross-platform efforts at supporting a product that could easily be Android (or Samsung) only. In my opinion, a watch shouldn’t be tied to a single ecosystem in order to to function.

I have found the S-Health app and Galaxy Watch to be accurate within about +/- 5-10% of my previous Fitbit models (which are not necessarily the gold standard anyways); and, the extra functionality here is really nice. Paired with the Galaxy Watch app also by Samsung, I am really enjoying my new smart watch!

title: Doesn’t Sync Steps/Sleep with UA Record
body:
Response to Developer:
I’m using the current version (1.5.0.035).

Another issue in finding while using S Health for now is that my dinner meals I enter tend to migrate to the next day on their own.  I delete it from today and add it back to yesterday, but it’ll end back up in today’s meals.

I’ve already put a ticket in with UA Record but feel the issue is more on S Health.  When in UA Record and tying to S Health, a window of the S Health app comes up prompting for my Samsung account credentials, after typing them in, its asking what permissions I want to provide.  It only defines Read/Write permissions for “Exercise”.  It does not list anything for “Steps or Sleep”.  Choosing the defaults (enabling read/write for Exercise) the integration between the two apps is complete and a sync is supposedly done.  But that’s not the case.  None of my sleep or step data transferred over.  

There is an option to change sync priorities, but when choosing that I can’t do anything. It shows I have multiple sources for sleep & step data but that’s not true as I had no other apps tied in.  I tried restarting my phone, reinstalling both apps, even deleting my UA Record account and creating a new one but nothing worked.  

Supposedly there’s “Data Permissions” that can be configured in S Health (per UA Record documentation) but that’s not the case.  Hoping for a resolution as this is supposed to work.

title: Three Major Bugs
body:
Premise: I really love this app!  I so appreciate the Samsung gear watch, and I love that it has an iOS version app.  I also love the ability to set goals, log food, and compete internationally with steps! All great things!! Without the following bugs, I would give this app 5 stars.

1) the app will misplace food entries, specifically putting yesterday's dinner/"evening snack" into today's log for dinner/"evening snack".  It is very frustrating to have to reprogram meals into previous days; I often have to do it two or three times before it sticks!  Very bad.

2) the app immediately crashes when I try to access my physical goal (one of the top wheels in the upper left corner that keeps track of my total activity of the day in terms of minutes).  The screen goes black and returns me to my home screen :/ extremely frustrating.

3) I am unable to write a comment/complaint to Samsung directly through the app.  Every time I try, the message either refuses to send or the app itself crashes.  I have tried different internet sources, resetting my whole phone, refreshing the app -- nothing allows for me to send communication over these problems directly to the app creator :/ 

Please note: my iOS system is up to date as of two days ago, and problems persist/worsen.  My phone is iPhone 6 gen.  I have the latest update for the Samsung app.

I hope to update my review of this app if/when these bugs are fixed.  I hope to hear from the Samsung team soon.  Thank you.

3. total calories burnt as seen on Watch are no where to be found on app

I’ve never written app reviews before, but the S Health app works extremely poorly on the iPhone. I have (am) seriously considered returning the watch because the app is useless to me. I (for a minimum) need to see:

calories burnt per day
distance walked per day
steps taken per day (though that seems to work)
total minutes active per day

I have stopped using the app. I’m on the lookout for updates, hoping these issues will be solved at some point soon, since I do like the watch.

Now that I have a provisioned iOS device I have switched to Apple Watch and have been waiting for this app to release so I could get back to competing with friends. It’s extremely disappointing that the initial release doesn’t support data input from the most widely used iOS tracking device. I look forward to future updates from Samsung to add compatibility.

title: What a shame!!!
body: I own the new gear sport and I have nothing but great things to talk about it. The Samsung health app on the other hand is such a joke. Even the MSFT band app is so much better than this. So don’t blame it on the iOS restrictions. After a week of use, I switched phones. The watch indicated that the data will be reset. I was under the impression that all the health data is stored on Samsung cloud since the app was connected to my Samsung account. Guess what?? Nothing showed up in the health app after I paired the new phone with the watch even after connecting to the Samsung account. Later on I found some sync setting under my account which was turned off by default. I can live with the lost data. After 2 days of use I synced the app. All the data from today appeared in the app. But nothing from yesterday. I tried manually syncing again. No dice. No idea what is going on. As a cherry on top, the app started to crash randomly. Great job!!!
